title: Verbs of Change in Urban & Housing Analysis

sections.content: You know *ponerse*, *volverse*, *hacerse*, *quedarse* and *convertirse en* from B1 Unit 25, B1 Unit 39 and B2 Unit 22 for personal changes. In urban reporting, these same verbs describe how neighbourhoods, rents and housing markets evolve, but each chooses a different angle: *volverse* + adjective marks a deep, lasting change that happens to a thing (*el alquiler se ha vuelto inalcanzable*); *quedarse* + adjective or *sin* + noun highlights a resulting state after a process or loss (*varias calles se han quedado despobladas*, *muchos inquilinos se quedaron sin vivienda*); *convertirse en* + noun signals a complete change of category (*el antiguo distrito industrial se convirtió en una zona de lujo*); and *hacerse* + adjective expresses a change that builds up over time (*el gasto se ha hecho insostenible*).

sections.title: Choosing the verb of change for urban processes
rows: Deep, lasting change that happens to a thing (*El mercado inmobiliario se ha vuelto inaccesible.*).
Resulting state after departure or loss (*El centro se quedó despoblado por la noche.*).
Full change of identity or role (*El barrio se convirtió en una zona de lujo.*).
Change that builds up over time (*Pagar el alquiler se ha hecho insostenible.*).

items.spanish: Con la especulación inmobiliaria, el alquiler en el área metropolitana se ha vuelto inaccesible para muchos jóvenes.
items.english: With property speculation, rent in the metropolitan area has become inaccessible for many young people.

items.spanish: Tras varios desalojos, dos calles enteras se quedaron despobladas durante meses.
items.english: After several evictions, two whole streets were left depopulated for months.

items.spanish: En quince años, el viejo barrio portuario se convirtió en un centro comercial de alto precio.
items.english: In fifteen years, the old port district turned into a high-priced commercial centre.

items.spanish: Para muchos inquilinos, renovar el contrato en el centro se ha hecho insostenible.
items.english: For many tenants, renewing the lease in the centre has become unsustainable.

sections.content: Avoid *ponerse* for long-term urban or economic trends: *ponerse* fits temporary states or sudden moods (*el tráfico se puso terrible*), not structural shifts. Use *volverse* or *hacerse* for lasting market changes, and *convertirse en* when something turns into something else.
